**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of the *National Health (Listing of Pharmaceutical Benefits) Instrument 2024* that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 1 September 2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the ***endnotes***) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Editorial changes**

For more information about any editorial changes made in this compilation, see the endnotes.

**Presentational changes**

The *Legislation Act 2003* provides for First Parliamentary Counsel to make presentational changes to a compilation. Presentational changes are applied to give a more consistent look and feel to legislation published on the Register, and enable the user to more easily navigate those documents.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self‑repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

Contents

### Part 1—Preliminary

###### 1 Name

(1) This instrument is the *National Health (Listing of Pharmaceutical Benefits) Instrument 2024*.

(2) This instrument may also be cited as PB 26 of 2024.

###### 3 Authority

This instrument is made under sections 84AF, 84AK, 85, 85A and 88 of the *National Health Act 1953*.

###### 4 Simplified outline

This instrument deals with a number of different matters concerning pharmaceutical benefits.

Part 2 defines pharmaceutical benefits, by identifying the drugs and medicinal preparations to which Part VII of the Act applies, and the forms, manners of administration and brands for those drugs and medicinal preparations. It also identifies the responsible person for brands and which brands are treated as equivalent to each other.

Part 3 deals with the rules for prescribing pharmaceutical benefits, including who can write prescriptions and the maximum quantities and number of repeats that can be prescribed.

Part 4 defines quantities of pharmaceutical benefits that are used for pricing purposes.

Part 5 identifies drugs and pharmaceutical benefits that can only be supplied in particular ways.

###### 5 Definitions

Note 1: A number of expressions used in this instrument are defined in the Act, including the following:

(a) Chief Executive Medicare;

(b) hospital.

Note 2: Under subsection 4(1A) of the Act, a word or phrase defined for the purposes of the *Health Insurance Act 1973* has the meaning that it would have if used in that Act. Expressions used in this instrument that are defined in that Act include the following:

(a) medical practitioner;

(b) medicare benefit.

In this instrument:

***ABN*** has the same meaning as in the *A New Tax System (Australian Business Number) Act 1999*.

***Act*** means the *National Health Act 1953*.

***authorised midwife*** has the same meaning as in Part VII of the Act.

***authorised nurse practitioner*** has the same meaning as in Part VII of the Act.

***authorised optometrist*** has the same meaning as in Part VII of the Act.

***authorised prescriber***, of a pharmaceutical benefit, means a PBS prescriber (within the meaning of Part VII of the Act) who is authorised under section 12 of this instrument to write a prescription for the supply of the benefit.

***brand***, of a pharmaceutical item, has the same meaning as in Part VII of the Act.

***CFC*** is short for chlorofluorocarbon.

***CFU*** is short for colony forming unit.

***circumstances code*** means the letter “C” followed by a number.

***conditions code*** means the letters “CN” followed by a number.

***extemporaneously‑prepared pharmaceutical benefit*** means a pharmaceutical benefit that:

(a) is a listed drug mentioned in column 1 of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 2; or

(b) contains such a listed drug.

***General statement for drugs for the treatment of hepatitis C*** means the statement set out in Schedule 6.

***GP Management Plan*** means a comprehensive written plan for the treatment of a patient:

(a) that is prepared by a medical practitioner; and

(b) for the preparation of which a medicare benefit is payable; and

(c) that includes a description of the patient’s health care needs, management goals, actions to be taken by the patient, and treatment and services the patient is likely to need.

***I.M.*** is short for intramuscular.

***I.U.*** is short for international unit.

***I.V.*** is short for intravenous.

***listed drug*** has the same meaning as in Part VII of the Act.

***Medicare Benefits Schedule*** means:

(a) the table, within the meaning of subsection 3(1) of the *Health Insurance Act 1973*; or

(b) any determination made under subsection 3C(1) of that Act.

***palliative care patient*** means a patient with an active, progressive, far‑advanced disease for whom the prognosis is limited and the focus of care is the quality of life.

***participating dental practitioner*** has the same meaning as in Part VII of the Act.

***pharmaceutical benefit*** has the same meaning as in Part VII of the Act.

***pharmaceutical item*** has the same meaning as in Part VII of the Act.

***purposes code*** means the letter “P” followed by a number.

***ready‑prepared pharmaceutical benefit*** means a pharmaceutical benefit that is mentioned in a table in Schedule 1.

***streamlined authority code*** means the words “Streamlined Authority Code” followed by a number.

***Team Care Arrangements*** means arrangements:

(a) that are coordinated by a medical practitioner; and

(b) for the coordination of which a medicare benefit is payable; and

(c) that, following consultation with collaborating providers, are documented in a plan that includes a description of the treatment and service goals for the patient, the treatment and services that all collaborating providers will provide, and the actions to be taken by the patient.

***variation code*** means the letter “V” followed by a number.

### Part 2—Pharmaceutical benefits

###### 6 Drugs and medicinal preparations to which Part VII of the Act applies (Act s 85(2))

Drugs and medicinal preparations—Schedule 1

(1) For the purposes of paragraph 85(2)(a) of the Act, Part VII of the Act applies to a drug or medicinal preparation mentioned in the column of a table in Schedule 1 to this instrument headed “Listed Drug”.

Drugs and medicinal preparations—Schedule 2

(2) For the purposes of paragraph 85(2)(a) of the Act, Part VII of the Act applies to:

(a) a drug or medicinal preparation mentioned in column 1 of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 2 to this instrument; and

(b) a medicinal preparation composed of one or more drugs or medicinal preparations mentioned in that column.

(3) For the purposes of paragraph 85(2)(b) of the Act, that paragraph applies to:

(a) the class of drugs and medicinal preparations consisting of the drugs and medicinal preparations mentioned in column 1 of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 2 to this instrument; and

(b) additives mentioned in the table in Part 2 of that Schedule.

Note: Part VII of the Act applies to medicinal preparations composed of one or more of the drugs and medicinal preparations included in the class mentioned in paragraph (a) of this subsection and one or more additives mentioned in paragraph (b) of this subsection—see paragraph 85(2)(b) of the Act.

###### 7 Form or forms of a listed drug (Act s 85(3))

For the purposes of subsection 85(3) of the Act, the form or forms of a listed drug mentioned in a table in Schedule 1 to this instrument are the form or forms mentioned in relation to the listed drug in the column of the table headed “Form”.

###### 8 Manner of administration of a form of a listed drug (Act s 85(5))

For the purposes of subsection 85(5) of the Act, the manner of administration of a form of a listed drug mentioned in a table in Schedule 1 to this instrument is the manner of administration mentioned in relation to the form of the drug in the column of the table headed “Manner of Administration”.

###### 9 Brand of a pharmaceutical item (Act s 85(6))

For the purposes of subsection 85(6) of the Act, each brand mentioned in the column of a table in Schedule 1 to this instrument headed “Brand” in relation to a pharmaceutical item is a brand of the pharmaceutical item.

###### 10 Responsible person for a brand of a pharmaceutical item (Act s 84AF(1))

For the purposes of subsection 84AF(1) of the Act, the responsible person for a brand of a pharmaceutical item mentioned in a table in Schedule 1 to this instrument is the person represented, in accordance with the table in Schedule 3, by the code mentioned in relation to the brand in the column of the table in Schedule 1 headed “Responsible Person”.

###### 11 Schedule equivalents of brands of pharmaceutical items (Act s 85(6A))

For the purposes of subsection 85(6A) of the Act, a brand of a pharmaceutical item included in a schedule equivalent group in the table in Schedule 5 to this instrument is, for the purposes of paragraph 103(2A)(b) of the Act, to be treated as equivalent to each other brand of a pharmaceutical item that is included in that schedule equivalent group.

Extemporaneously‑prepared pharmaceutical benefits

(2) For the purposes of subsection 88(1) of the Act, a medical practitioner is authorised to write a prescription for the supply of an extemporaneously‑prepared pharmaceutical benefit.

###### 13 Prescription of ready‑prepared pharmaceutical benefits in certain circumstances (Act s 85(7))

For the purposes of paragraphs 85(7)(a) and (b) of the Act, if a circumstances code is mentioned in the column of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 1 to this instrument headed “Circumstances” in relation to a pharmaceutical benefit:

(a) the pharmaceutical benefit is a relevant pharmaceutical benefit for the purposes of section 88A of the Act; and

(b) the circumstances mentioned in the column of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 4 to this instrument headed “Circumstances and Purposes” in relation to the circumstances code are circumstances in which a prescription for the supply of the pharmaceutical benefit may be written; and

(c) if the column of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 4 to this instrument headed “Authority Requirements” in relation to the circumstances code is not blank—it is part of the circumstances that writing the prescription must be authorised by the Chief Executive Medicare in accordance with section 19 of this instrument.

###### 14 Prescription of extemporaneously‑prepared pharmaceutical benefits in certain circumstances (Act s 85(7))

(1) If circumstances are mentioned in column 2 of an item in the table in Part 1 of Schedule 2, then:

(a) for the purposes of paragraph 85(7)(a) of the Act:

(i) the listed drug mentioned in column 1 of the item is a relevant pharmaceutical benefit for the purposes of section 88A of the Act; and

(ii) an extemporaneously‑prepared pharmaceutical benefit that contains the listed drug is a relevant pharmaceutical benefit for the purposes of section 88A of the Act; and

(b) for the purposes of paragraph 85(7)(b) of the Act, the circumstances are circumstances in which a prescription may be written:

(i) for the supply of the listed drug; or

(ii) for the supply of a pharmaceutical benefit that is a relevant pharmaceutical benefit under subparagraph (a)(ii) of this subsection only because it contains the listed drug.

(2) If a pharmaceutical benefit contains 2 or more listed drugs that are relevant pharmaceutical benefits under subparagraph (1)(a)(i) (the ***component drugs***), then, for the purposes of paragraph 85(7)(b) of the Act, a prescription for the supply of the pharmaceutical benefit may be written only if the circumstances mentioned in column 2 of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 2 to this instrument for every component drug exist.

#### Division 2—Maximum quantities and repeats

###### 15 Maximum quantity (number of units)—ready‑prepared pharmaceutical benefits (Act s 85A(2)(a), (2A) and (3A))

Purpose of section

(1) This section determines, with respect to the writing of prescriptions for the supply of a ready‑prepared pharmaceutical benefit having a pharmaceutical item by authorised prescribers of the benefit:

(a) for the purposes of paragraph 85A(2)(a) of the Act—the maximum number of units of the pharmaceutical item that may, in one prescription, be directed to be supplied on any one occasion; and

(b) for the purposes of subsection 85A(2A) of the Act—conditions that must be satisfied when writing a prescription; and

(c) for the purposes of subsection 85A(3A) of the Act—rules that must be applied when deciding whether to authorise a variation of the application of a determination referred to in paragraph (a) of this subsection.

Determination of maximum number of units

(2) If only one number of units is mentioned in the column of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 1 to this instrument headed “Maximum Quantity” in relation to brands of the pharmaceutical item and a kind of authorised prescriber, that number of units is the maximum number of units of the pharmaceutical item for that kind of authorised prescriber for all purposes.

(3) If more than one number of units is mentioned in the column of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 1 headed “Maximum Quantity” in relation to brands of the pharmaceutical item and a kind of authorised prescriber, then:

(a) if a purposes code is mentioned in the column of the table headed “Purposes” in relation to a number of units—that number is the maximum number of units of the pharmaceutical item for that kind of authorised prescriber for the purposes mentioned in the table in Part 1 of Schedule 4 for that purposes code; and

(b) if no purposes code is mentioned in that column in relation to a number of units—that number is the maximum number of units of the pharmaceutical item for that kind of authorised prescriber for all purposes other than purposes to which paragraph (a) applies.

Conditions for writing prescription

(4) If the column of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 1 headed “Maximum Quantity” includes a conditions code together with a maximum number of units, it is a condition when writing a prescription to which that maximum applies that writing the prescription must be authorised by the Chief Executive Medicare in accordance with section 19 of this instrument.

Rules for authorising variation of maximum number of units

(5) If the column of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 1 headed “Variations” includes a variation code in relation to a maximum number of units, the rules mentioned in the column of the table in Part 2 of Schedule 4 headed “Variation Rules” in relation to the variation code must be applied when deciding whether to authorise a variation of that maximum (to the extent that those rules relate to the number of units).

Note: Rules may also relate to the maximum number of repeats.

###### 16 Maximum number of repeats—ready‑prepared pharmaceutical benefits (Act s 85A(2)(b), (2A) and (3A))

Purpose of section

(1) This section determines, with respect to the writing of prescriptions for the supply of a ready‑prepared pharmaceutical benefit by authorised prescribers of the benefit:

(a) for the purposes of paragraph 85A(2)(b) of the Act—the maximum number of occasions on which the supply of the pharmaceutical benefit may, in one prescription, be directed to be repeated; and

(b) for the purposes of subsection 85A(2A) of the Act—conditions that must be satisfied when writing a prescription; and

(c) for the purposes of subsection 85A(3A) of the Act—rules that must be applied when deciding whether to authorise a variation of the application of a determination referred to in paragraph (a) of this subsection.

Determination of maximum number of repeats

(2) If only one number is mentioned in the column of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 1 to this instrument headed “Number of Repeats” in relation to the pharmaceutical benefit and a kind of authorised prescriber, that number is the maximum number of occasions for that kind of authorised prescriber for all purposes.

(3) If more than one number is mentioned in the column of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 1 headed “Number of Repeats” in relation to the pharmaceutical benefit and a kind of authorised prescriber, then:

(a) if a purposes code is mentioned in the column of the table headed “Purposes” in relation to a number—that number is the maximum number of occasions for that kind of authorised prescriber for the purposes mentioned in the table in Part 1 of Schedule 4 for that purposes code; and

(b) if no purposes code is mentioned in that column in relation to a number—that number is the maximum number of occasions for that kind of authorised prescriber for all purposes other than purposes to which paragraph (a) applies.

Conditions for writing prescription

(4) If the column of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 1 headed “Number of Repeats” includes a conditions code together with a maximum number of occasions that supply may be directed to be repeated, it is a condition when writing a prescription to which that maximum applies that writing the prescription must be authorised by the Chief Executive Medicare in accordance with section 19 of this instrument.

Rules for authorising variation of maximum number of repeats

(5) If the column of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 1 headed “Variations” includes a variation code in relation to a maximum number of repeats, the rules mentioned in the column of the table in Part 2 of Schedule 4 headed “Variation Rules” in relation to the variation code must be applied when deciding whether to authorise a variation of that maximum (to the extent that those rules relate to the number of repeats).

Note: Rules may also relate to the maximum number of units.

###### 17 Maximum quantity—extemporaneously‑prepared pharmaceutical benefits (Act s 85A(2)(a))

For the purposes of paragraph 85A(2)(a) of the Act, the maximum quantity of an extemporaneously‑prepared pharmaceutical benefit, of a type mentioned in column 1 of an item in the table in Part 3 of Schedule 2 to this instrument, that a medical practitioner may, in one prescription, direct to be supplied on any one occasion is the quantity mentioned in column 2 of the item.

###### 18 Maximum number of repeats—extemporaneously‑prepared pharmaceutical benefits (Act s 85A(2)(b))

For the purposes of paragraph 85A(2)(b) of the Act, the maximum number of occasions that a medical practitioner may, in one prescription, direct that the supply of an extemporaneously‑prepared pharmaceutical benefit, of a type mentioned in column 1 of an item in the table in Part 3 of Schedule 2 to this instrument, be repeated is the number mentioned in column 3 of the item.

#### Division 3—Authorisation of prescriptions

###### 19 Authority required procedures

(1) This section applies if:

(a) the circumstances under paragraph 85(7)(b) of the Act in which a prescription for the supply of a pharmaceutical benefit may be written; or

(b) the conditions under subsection 85A(2A) of the Act for writing a prescription for the supply of a pharmaceutical benefit;

include a requirement that writing the prescription must be authorised by the Chief Executive Medicare.

Obtaining authority

(2) When requesting authority to write a prescription, an authorised prescriber must provide details of the proposed prescription to the Chief Executive Medicare.

(3) If the column of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 4 to this instrument headed “Authority Requirements” contains the statement “Compliance with Written Authority Required procedures”, the details must be provided in writing.

(4) If the Chief Executive Medicare gives authority to write the prescription, the Chief Executive Medicare must allot a number to the prescription and tell the authorised prescriber that number.

Note: For requirements to write the allotted number on the prescription, see sections 40 and 41 of the *National Health (Pharmaceutical Benefits) Regulations 2017*.

Deemed authority

(5) If the column of the table in Part 1 of Schedule 4 headed “Authority Requirements” includes a streamlined authority code, writing the prescription is taken to have been authorised by the Chief Executive Medicare.

Note: For requirements to write the streamlined authority code on the prescription, see sections 40 and 41 of the *National Health (Pharmaceutical Benefits) Regulations 2017*.

### Part 4—Quantities of pharmaceutical items

###### 20 Pack quantity (Act s 84AK(2))

For the purposes of subsection 84AK(2) of the Act, a number of units of a pharmaceutical item mentioned in the column of a table in Schedule 1 to this instrument headed “Pack Quantity” in relation to a brand of the pharmaceutical item is a pack quantity of the brand.

###### 21 Determined quantity (Act s 84AK(3))

For the purposes of subsection 84AK(3) of the Act, a number of units of a pharmaceutical item mentioned in the column of a table in Schedule 1 to this instrument headed “Determined Quantity” in relation to a brand of the pharmaceutical item is a determined quantity of the brand.

### Part 5—Supply of pharmaceutical benefits

###### 22 Listed drugs and pharmaceutical benefits that can only be supplied under the prescriber bag provisions (Act s 85(2AA) and (7A))

Listed drugs

(1) For the purposes of subsection 85(2AA) of the Act, if one or more of the codes “D(MP)”, “D(MW)” and “D(NP)” are mentioned in the column of a table in Schedule 1 to this instrument headed “Section 100/Prescriber Bag only” in relation to a listed drug, then the listed drug can only be supplied under:

(a) if the code D(MP) is mentioned—section 93 of the Act (prescriber bag supplies—medical practitioners); and

(b) if the code D(MW) is mentioned—section 93AA of the Act (prescriber bag supplies—authorised midwives); and

(c) if the code D(NP) is mentioned—section 93AB of the Act (prescriber bag supplies—authorised nurse practitioners).

Pharmaceutical benefits

(2) For the purposes of subsection 85(7A) of the Act, if one or more of the codes “PB(MP)”, “PB(MW)” and “PB(NP)” are mentioned in the column of a table in Schedule 1 to this instrument headed “Section 100/Prescriber Bag only” in relation to a pharmaceutical benefit, then the pharmaceutical benefit can only be supplied in accordance with the following:

(a) if the code PB(MP) is mentioned—section 93 of the Act (prescriber bag supplies—medical practitioners);

(b) if the code PB(MW) is mentioned—section 93AA of the Act (prescriber bag supplies—authorised midwives);

(c) if the code PB(NP) is mentioned—section 93AB of the Act (prescriber bag supplies—authorised nurse practitioners).

Note: For the interaction between a declaration under subsection 85(2AA) of the Act in relation to a drug and a declaration under subsection 85(7A) of the Act in relation to a pharmaceutical benefit that has the drug, see subsection 85AAA(3) of the Act.

###### 23 Listed drugs and pharmaceutical benefits that can be supplied only under special arrangements (Act s 85(2A) and (8))

Listed drugs

(1) For the purposes of subsection 85(2A) of the Act, a listed drug can be supplied only under special arrangements under section 100 of the Act if the code “D(100)” is mentioned in the column of a table in Schedule 1 to this instrument headed “Section 100/Prescriber Bag only” in relation to the drug.

Pharmaceutical benefits

(2) For the purposes of paragraph 85(8)(a) of the Act, a ready‑prepared pharmaceutical benefit can be supplied only under special arrangements under section 100 of the Act if the code “PB(100)” is mentioned in the column of a table in Schedule 1 to this instrument headed “Section 100/Prescriber Bag only” in relation to the pharmaceutical benefit.

Circumstances

(3) For the purposes of paragraph 85(8)(b) of the Act, if the code “C(100)” is mentioned in the column of a table in Schedule 1 to this instrument headed “Section 100/Prescriber Bag only” in relation to a pharmaceutical benefit and a circumstances code, the circumstances mentioned in the table in Part 1 of Schedule 4 for the circumstances code are circumstances in which the pharmaceutical benefit can be supplied only under special arrangements under section 100 of the Act.

### Part 6—Application, saving and transitional provisions

###### 24 Transitional provision—authorisation of prescriptions

(1) This section applies in relation to prescriptions for the supply of pharmaceutical benefits written before 1 July 2024.

(2) Despite the repeal of the *National Health (Listing of Pharmaceutical Benefits) Instrument 2012*:

(a) an authorised prescriber may submit a prescription to the Chief Executive Medicare in accordance with section 12 of that instrument as in force immediately before 1 April 2024; and

(b) the Chief Executive Medicare may authorise the prescription in accordance with section 13 of that instrument as in force immediately before 1 April 2024; and

(c) if the prescription is so authorised, writing the prescription is taken to have been authorised in accordance with section 19 of this instrument.

(3) If the Chief Executive Medicare authorises a prescription under subsection 13(1), (1A) or (1B) of the *National Health (Listing of Pharmaceutical Benefits) Instrument 2012* as in force immediately before 1 April 2024, the authorised prescriber is not required to comply with the following provisions of the *National Health (Pharmaceutical Benefits) Regulations 2017* in relation to the prescription:

(a) paragraph 40(1)(i);

(b) paragraph 41(3)(a).

**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of the *National Health (Listing of Pharmaceutical Benefits) Instrument 2024* that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 1 September 2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the ***endnotes***) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the

**Uncommenced amendments**

compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Editorial changes**

For more information about any editorial changes made in this compilation, see the endnotes.

**Presentational changes**

The *Legislation Act 2003* provides for First Parliamentary Counsel to make presentational changes to a compilation. Presentational changes are applied to give a more consistent look and feel to legislation published on the Register, and enable the user to more easily navigate those documents.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self‑repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of the *National Health (Listing of Pharmaceutical Benefits) Instrument 2024* that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 1 September 2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the ***endnotes***) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Editorial changes**

For more information about any editorial changes made in this compilation, see the endnotes.

**Presentational changes**

The *Legislation Act 2003* provides for First Parliamentary Counsel to make presentational changes to a compilation. Presentational changes are applied to give a more consistent look and feel to legislation published on the Register, and enable the user to more easily navigate those documents.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self‑repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of the *National Health (Listing of Pharmaceutical Benefits) Instrument 2024* that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 1 September 2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the ***endnotes***) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Editorial changes**

For more information about any editorial changes made in this compilation, see the endnotes.

**Presentational changes**

The *Legislation Act 2003* provides for First Parliamentary Counsel to make presentational changes to a compilation. Presentational changes are applied to give a more consistent look and feel to legislation published on the Register, and enable the user to more easily navigate those documents.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self‑repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

The matters determined for the pharmaceutical benefit in this instrument relate to its general supply under Part VII of the Act, and may be modified in the special arrangement instrument. When the pharmaceutical benefit is supplied under the special arrangement, the modified matters will apply.

Note 3: This matter has not been determined for the pharmaceutical benefit in this instrument. The pharmaceutical benefit can only be supplied, or can only be supplied in the circumstances mentioned, under special arrangements under section 100 of the Act. The matter may be determined in a special arrangement instrument.

Note 4: The pharmaceutical benefit may be supplied only under the particular prescriber bag provisions of the Act indicated by the code or codes in the column headed 'Section 100/Prescriber Bag only'. It is not able to be prescribed as a pharmaceutical benefit. The maximum quantity of the pharmaceutical benefit that may be obtained by the particular prescriber for direct supply from their prescriber bag is determined in a legislative instrument made under the relevant prescriber bag provisions of the Act (sections 93, 93AA and 93AB).

**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of the *National Health (Listing of Pharmaceutical Benefits) Instrument 2024* that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 1 September 2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the ***endnotes***) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Editorial changes**

For more information about any editorial changes made in this compilation, see the endnotes.

**Presentational changes**

The *Legislation Act 2003* provides for First Parliamentary Counsel to make presentational changes to a compilation. Presentational changes are applied to give a more consistent look and feel to legislation published on the Register, and enable the user to more easily navigate those documents.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self‑repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of the *National Health (Listing of Pharmaceutical Benefits) Instrument 2024* that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 1 September 2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the ***endnotes***) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Editorial changes**

For more information about any editorial changes made in this compilation, see the endnotes.

**Presentational changes**

The *Legislation Act 2003* provides for First Parliamentary Counsel to make presentational changes to a compilation. Presentational changes are applied to give a more consistent look and feel to legislation published on the Register, and enable the user to more easily navigate those documents.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self‑repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

###### 1 Circumstances, purposes and conditions

The following table sets out:

(b) purposes for purposes codes, for the purposes of sections 15 and 16; and

| C10020 | P10020 | CN10020 | Risperidone | Behavioural disturbances<br>Initial treatment<br>The condition must be characterised by psychotic symptoms and aggression; AND<br>Patient must have dementia of the Alzheimer type; AND<br>Patient must have failed to respond to non-pharmacological methods of treatment; AND<br>Patient must not receive more than 12 weeks of treatment under this restriction.<br>A patient may only qualify for 12 weeks of PBS-subsidised treatment under this restriction once in a 12 month period. | Compliance with Authority Required procedures - Streamlined Authority Code 10020 |
| C10021 | P10021 | CN10021 | Risperidone | Behavioural disturbances<br>Continuing treatment, trial of dose reduction or cessation of treatment<br>The condition must be characterised by psychotic symptoms and aggression; AND<br>Patient must have dementia of the Alzheimer type; AND<br>Patient must have responded to an initial course of treatment with this drug for this condition; AND<br>Patient must have failed to respond to non-pharmacological methods of treatment; AND<br>The treatment must be for dose tapering purposes as part of a trial of treatment reduction or cessation; or<br>Patient must have trialled a period of treatment reduction or cessation with this drug for this condition and experienced worsening or re-emergence of symptoms during this trial, and retrials are considered periodically; AND<br>Patient must be optimised on non-pharmacological methods of treatment.<br>The patient's response to treatment and a trial of treatment reduction or cessation must be discussed formally with a psychiatrist or geriatrician or in a documented clinical review process involving a least one other medical practitioner, or be reviewed by a psychiatrist or geriatrician.<br>Response to treatment is defined as a significant reduction in symptoms of psychosis or aggression.<br>Patients must cease treatment if there is no improvement in symptoms of psychosis and aggression, or worsening of symptoms with therapy.<br>Patients must be monitored for adverse effects such as falls, drowsiness leading to reduced self-care, incontinence, reduced nutrition, reduced ability to communicate needs/wishes and take part in activities. Therapy must be ceased if harms of therapy outweigh benefits.<br>Trials of reduction or cessation of therapy should be considered periodically with the intention of maintaining symptom control through non-pharmacological measures wherever possible and/or lowest effective dose therapy.<br>Evidence of patient benefit from therapy, failure of non-pharmacological approaches to manage symptoms in the absence of therapy, and recurrence of symptoms following reduction or cessation of therapy, trialled on at least 1 occasion, must be documented in the patient's medical records. | Compliance with Authority Required procedures |

| C10063 | P10063 | CN10063 | Cinacalcet | Secondary hyperparathyroidism<br>Continuing treatment<br>Must be treated by a nephrologist; AND<br>Patient must have chronic kidney disease; AND<br>Patient must be on dialysis; AND<br>Patient must have previously received PBS-subsidised treatment with this drug for this condition.<br>During the maintenance phase, iPTH should be monitored quarterly (measured at least 12 hours post dose) and dose adjusted as necessary to maintain an appropriate iPTH concentration.<br>During the maintenance phase, prescribers should request approval to allow sufficient supply for 4 weeks treatment up to a maximum of 6 months supply, with doses between 30 and 180 mg per day according to the patient's response and tolerability. | Compliance with Authority Required procedures - Streamlined Authority Code 10063 |

**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of the *National Health (Listing of Pharmaceutical Benefits) Instrument 2024* that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 1 September 2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the ***endnotes***) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Editorial changes**

For more information about any editorial changes made in this compilation, see the endnotes.

**Presentational changes**

The *Legislation Act 2003* provides for First Parliamentary Counsel to make presentational changes to a compilation. Presentational changes are applied to give a more consistent look and feel to legislation published on the Register, and enable the user to more easily navigate those documents.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self‑repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

| C13018 | P13018 | CN13018 | Pertuzumab | Metastatic (Stage IV) HER2 positive breast cancer<br>Initial treatment<br>Patient must have evidence of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) gene amplification as demonstrated by in situ hybridisation (ISH) either in the primary tumour or a metastatic lesion, confirmed through a pathology report from an Approved Pathology Authority; AND<br>Patient must have a WHO performance status of 0 or 1; AND<br>Patient must not have received prior anti-HER2 therapy for this condition; AND<br>Patient must not have received prior chemotherapy for this condition; AND<br>The treatment must be in combination with trastuzumab and a taxane; AND<br>The treatment must not be in combination with nab-paclitaxel; AND<br>The treatment must not be used in a patient with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of less than 45% and/or with symptomatic heart failure.<br>Details (date, unique identifying number/code, or provider number) of the pathology report from an Approved Pathology Authority confirming evidence of HER2 gene amplification in the primary tumour or a metastatic lesion by in situ hybridisation (ISH) must be provided at the time of application.<br>The pathology report must be documented in the patient's medical records.<br>Cardiac function must be tested by echocardiography (ECHO) or multigated acquisition (MUGA), prior to seeking the initial authority approval. | Compliance with Authority Required procedures |
| C13040 | P13040 | CN13040 | Infliximab | Severe psoriatic arthritis<br>Balance of supply (including switching formulation) where the full duration of treatment available under a particular treatment phase was not requested in the preceding prescription<br>Must be treated by a rheumatologist; or<br>Must be treated by a clinical immunologist with expertise in the management of psoriatic arthritis; AND<br>Patient must be undergoing continuing PBS-subsidised treatment with this benefit, irrespective of formulation, where each of the following is true:<br>(i) the most recent authority application did not specify the full quantity of repeat prescriptions available under the relevant PBS listing, (ii) this authority application does not extend the current treatment phase beyond that available under the listing of the most recent authority application, (iii) this Balance of Supply listing is not being accessed on consecutive occasions; or<br>Patient must be undergoing continuing PBS-subsidised treatment with this benefit, irrespective of formulation, where each of the following is true:<br>(i) the most recent authority application was for a different formulation of this benefit, (ii) this authority application does not extend the current treatment phase beyond that available under the listing of the most recent authority application, (iii) this Balance of Supply listing is not being accessed on consecutive occasions;<br>Patient must be at least 18 years of age.<br>Where there is a current, approved PBS prescription with valid repeat prescriptions specified (i.e. where the drug formulation is changing), mark the prescription that is intended for no further supply as 'Cancelled'. | Compliance with Authority Required procedures |
| C13045 | P13045 | CN13045 | Infliximab | Moderate to severe ulcerative colitis<br>Initial treatment with the subcutaneous form where a concurrent PBS authority application for the intravenously (IV) administered formulation is being made<br>Must be treated by a specialist prescriber who is the same prescriber completing the PBS authority application for the IV administered formulation of this drug/biological medicine; AND<br>Patient must be undergoing treatment with this benefit where:<br>(i) there is a concurrent PBS authority application for the IV administered formulation submitted for approval, (ii) the concurrent PBS authority application is approved/in the process of being approved;<br>Patient must be at least 18 years of age.<br>The authority application must be made in writing and must include<br>(1) a completed authority prescription form; and<br>(2) a completed authority application form relevant to the indication and treatment phase (the latest version is located on the website specified in the Administrative Advice).<br>The PBS administrator will confirm that<br>(i) there is a concurrent authority application for the intravenous (IV) formulation of this benefit for the patient;<br>(ii) the concurrent authority application for the IV formulation is to be approved before approving this authority application. | Compliance with Authority Required procedures |

or<br>(f) at least a 25% increase in the size of an existing or the development of a new soft tissue plasmacytoma (determined by clinical examination or diagnostic imaging); or<br>(g) development of hypercalcaemia (corrected serum calcium greater than 2.65 mmol per L not attributable to any other cause).<br>Oligo-secretory and non-secretory patients are defined as having active disease with less than 10 g per L serum M protein.<br>Details of the histological diagnosis of multiple myeloma; (ii) leflunomide at a dose of at least 10 mg daily; (iii) sulfasalazine at a dose of at least 2 g daily; or<br>Patient must have failed, in the 24 months immediately prior to the date of the application, to achieve an adequate response to a trial of at least 6 months of intensive treatment with DMARDs which, if methotrexate is contraindicated according to the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA)-approved Product Information/cannot be tolerated at a 20 mg weekly dose, must include at least 3 months continuous treatment with at least 2 of the following DMARDs:<br>(i) hydroxychloroquine at a dose of at least 200 mg daily; (ii) leflunomide at a dose of at least 10 mg daily; (iii) sulfasalazine at a dose of at least 2 g daily; or<br>Patient must have failed, in the 24 months immediately prior to the date of the application, to achieve an adequate response to a trial of at least 3 months of continuous treatment with a DMARD where 2 of:<br>(i) hydroxychloroquine, (ii) leflunomide, (iii) sulfasalazine, are contraindicated according to the relevant TGA-approved Product Information/cannot be tolerated at the doses specified above in addition to having a contraindication or intolerance to methotrexate: the remaining tolerated DMARD must be trialled at a minimum dose as mentioned above; or<br>Patient must have a contraindication/severe intolerance to each of:<br>(i) methotrexate, (ii) hydroxychloroquine, (iii) leflunomide, (iv) sulfasalazine; in such cases, provide details of the contraindications/severe intolerances; AND<br>Patient must not receive more than 16 weeks of treatment under this restriction;<br>Patient must be at least 18 years of age.<br>If methotrexate is contraindicated according to the TGA-approved product information or cannot be tolerated at a 20 mg weekly dose, details of the contraindication or intolerance including severity to methotrexate must be provided at the time of application and documented in the patient's medical records. The maximum tolerated dose of methotrexate must be provided at the time of the application, if applicable, and documented in the patient's medical records.<br>The application must include details of the DMARDs trialled, their doses and duration of treatment, and all relevant contraindications and/or intolerances including severity.<br>The requirement to trial at least 2 DMARDs for periods of at least 3 months each can be met using single agents sequentially or by using one or more combinations of DMARDs, however the time on treatment must be at least 6 months.<br>If the requirement to trial 6 months of intensive DMARD therapy with at least 2 DMARDs cannot be met because of contraindications and/or intolerances of a severity necessitating permanent treatment withdrawal to all of the DMARDs specified above, details of the contraindication or intolerance including severity and dose for each DMARD must be provided at the time of application and documented in the patient's medical records.<br>The following criteria indicate failure to achieve an adequate response to DMARD treatment and must be demonstrated in all patients at the time of the initial application<br>an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) greater than 25 mm per hour and/or a C-reactive protein (CRP) level greater than 15 mg per L; AND either<br>(a) a total active joint count of at least 20 active (swollen and tender) joints; or<br>(b) at least 4 active joints from the following list of major joints<br>(i) elbow, wrist, knee and/or ankle (assessed as swollen and tender); and/or<br>(ii) shoulder and/or hip (assessed as pain in passive movement and restriction of passive movement, where pain and limitation of movement are due to active disease and not irreversible damage such as joint destruction or bony overgrowth).<br>The assessment of response to prior treatment must be documented in the patient's medical records.<br>The joint count and ESR and/or CRP must be determined at the completion of the 6 month intensive DMARD trial, but prior to ceasing DMARD therapy. All measures must be no more than 4 weeks old at the time of initial application.<br>If the requirement to demonstrate an elevated ESR or CRP cannot be met, the reasons why this criterion cannot be satisfied must be documented in the patient's medical records. Treatment with prednisolone dosed at 7.5 mg or higher daily (or equivalent) or a parenteral steroid within the past month (intramuscular or intravenous methylprednisolone or equivalent) is an acceptable reason.<br>Where the baseline active joint count is based on total active joints (i.e. more than 20 active joints), response must be determined according to the reduction in the total number of active joints. Where the baseline is determined on total number of major joints, the response must be determined on the total number of major joints. If only an ESR or CRP level is provided with the initial application, the same marker must be used to determine response.<br>The following information must be provided by the prescriber at the time of application and documented in the patient's medical records<br>(a) the active joint count, ESR and/or CRP result and date of results;<br>(b) details of prior treatment, including dose and date/duration of treatment.<br>(c) If applicable, details of any contraindications/intolerances.<br>(d) If applicable, the maximum tolerated dose of methotrexate.<br>An assessment of a patient's response to this initial course of treatment must be conducted following a minimum of 12 weeks of therapy and no later than 4 weeks prior the completion of this course of treatment.<br>Where a response assessment is not conducted within the required timeframe, the patient will be deemed to have failed to respond to treatment with this drug, unless the patient has experienced a serious adverse reaction of a severity resulting in the necessity for permanent withdrawal of treatment.<br>If a patient fails to demonstrate a response to treatment with this drug under this restriction they will not be eligible to receive further PBS-subsidised treatment with this drug for this condition. | Compliance with Authority Required procedures |

(ii) Grade III unilateral sacroiliitis; AND<br>Patient must have at least 2 of the following:<br>(i) low back pain and stiffness for 3 or more months that is relieved by exercise but not by rest; (ii) limitation of motion of the lumbar spine in the sagittal and the frontal planes as determined by a score of at least 1 on each of the lumbar flexion and lumbar side flexion measurements of the Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Metrology Index (BASMI); (iii) limitation of chest expansion relative to normal values for age and gender; AND<br>Patient must have a Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI) of at least 4 on a 0-10 scale that is no more than 4 weeks old at the time of application; or<br>Patient must have a clinical reason as to why demonstration of an elevated ESR or CRP cannot be met and the application must state the reason; AND<br>Patient must not receive more than 16 weeks of treatment under this restriction;<br>Patient must be at least 18 years of age;<br>Must be treated by a rheumatologist. or<br>Must be treated by a clinical immunologist with expertise in the management of ankylosing spondylitis.<br>The following must be provided at the time of application and documented in the patient's medical records<br>(i) details (name of the radiology report provider, date of the radiology report and unique identifying number/code that links report to the individual patient) of the radiological report confirming Grade II bilateral sacroiliitis or Grade III unilateral sacroiliitis; and<br>(ii) a baseline BASDAI score; and<br>(iii) a baseline ESR and/or CRP level.<br>To demonstrate a response to treatment the application must be accompanied with the assessment of response, conducted following a minimum of 12 weeks of therapy and no later than 4 weeks from cessation of the most recent course of biological medicine. It is recommended that an application for the continuing treatment be submitted no later than 4 weeks from the date of completion of the most recent course of treatment. This is to ensure treatment continuity for those who meet the continuing restriction.<br>Where a response assessment is not conducted within these timeframes, the patient will be deemed to have failed to respond to treatment with this drug.<br>If a patient fails to demonstrate a response to treatment with this drug they will not be eligible to receive further PBS-subsidised treatment with this drug for this condition within this treatment cycle. | C16151 | P16151 | CN16151 | Nivolumab with relatlimab | Unresectable Stage III or Stage IV malignant melanoma<br>Continuing treatment<br>Patient must have previously received PBS-subsidised treatment with this drug for this condition; AND<br>The treatment must be the sole PBS-subsidised therapy for this condition; AND<br>Patient must not have developed disease progression while receiving PBS-subsidised treatment with this drug for this condition.<br>Patients must only receive a maximum of 480 mg nivolumab and 160 mg relatlimab every four weeks under a flat dosing regimen.<br>The prescribed dose must be according to the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) Product Information.<br>The prescription must include the amount of nivolumab with relatlimab (Opdualag) that is appropriate to be prescribed for the patient. For the purposes of PBS subsidy, the maximum amount requested is based on the nivolumab dose only. The prescribed amount of nivolumab must be expressed in milligrams. | Compliance with Authority Required procedures - Streamlined Authority Code 16151 |
| C16155 | P16155 | CN16155 | Nirmatrelvir and ritonavir | SARS-CoV-2 infection<br>Patient must have received a positive nucleic acid test result; OR<br>Patient must have received a positive rapid antigen test (RAT) result; AND<br>Patient must not require hospitalisation for COVID-19 infection at the time of prescribing; AND<br>The treatment must be initiated within 5 days of symptom onset; OR<br>The treatment must be initiated as soon as possible after a diagnosis is confirmed where asymptomatic.<br>Patient must be at least 70 years of age.<br>Access to this drug through this restriction is permitted irrespective of vaccination status.<br>Where nucleic acid testing is used to confirm diagnosis, the result, testing date, location and test provider must be recorded on the patient record.<br>Where a RAT is used to confirm diagnosis, available information about the test result, testing date, location and test provider (where relevant) must be recorded on the patient record.<br>This drug is not PBS-subsidised for pre-exposure or post-exposure prophylaxis for the prevention of SARS-CoV-2 infection. | Compliance with Authority Required procedures - Streamlined Authority Code 16155 |
| C16156 | P16156 | CN16156 | Nirmatrelvir and ritonavir | SARS-CoV-2 infection<br>Patient must have received a positive nucleic acid test result; OR<br>Patient must have received a positive rapid antigen test (RAT) result; AND<br>Patient must have at least one sign or symptom attributable to COVID-19; AND<br>Patient must not require hospitalisation for COVID-19 infection at the time of prescribing; AND<br>The treatment must be initiated within 5 days of symptom onset.<br>Patient must be both: (i) at least 50 years of age, (ii) at high risk.<br>For the purpose of administering this restriction, high risk is defined as either a past COVID-19 infection episode resulting in hospitalisation, or the presence of at least two of the following conditions:<br>1. | C16180 | P16180 | CN16180 | Belzutifan | Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease<br>Continuing treatment<br>Patient must have previously received PBS-subsidised treatment with this drug for this condition for the same tumour type; AND<br>Patient must not have developed VHL-associated metastatic disease; AND<br>Patient must have demonstrated clinical improvement or stabilisation of the condition while being treated with this drug, the details of which must be kept with the patient's record; AND<br>The treatment must be the sole PBS-subsidised therapy for VHL disease associated tumours.<br>Must be treated by a physician with expertise in the management of VHL disease associated tumours.<br>Patients who cease therapy for reasons other than, clinical disease progression or metastasis, may re-initiate PBS-subsidised treatment through the initiating or recommencing treatment phase.<br>For the purpose of administering this restriction, clinical improvement or stabilisation of the patient's condition includes but is not limited to:<br>(i) avoidance of surgery;<br>(ii) avoidance of renal replacement therapy such as dialysis or renal transplantation in patients with VHL- associated renal cell carcinoma (RCC);<br>(iii) experiencing clinical benefit in at least one of the VHL associated conditions, as determined by the treating clinician(s). | Compliance with Authority Required procedures |

Post-transplant: solid organ (on immunosuppressive therapy), haematopoietic stem cell transplant (within 24 months),<br>c. Immunocompromised due to primary or acquired (HIV/AIDS) immunodeficiency; OR<br>2. Any significantly immunocompromising condition(s) where, in the last 3 months the patient has received:<br>a. Chemotherapy or whole body radiotherapy,<br>b. High-dose corticosteroids (at least 20 mg of prednisone per day, or equivalent) for at least 14 days in a month, or pulse corticosteroid therapy,<br>c. Biological agents and other treatments that deplete or inhibit B cell or T cell function (abatacept, anti-CD20 antibodies, BTK inhibitors, JAK inhibitors, sphingosine 1-phosphate receptor modulators, anti-CD52 antibodies, anti-complement antibodies, anti-thymocyte globulin),<br>d. Selected conventional synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) including mycophenolate, methotrexate, leflunomide, azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine (at least 1.5mg/kg/day), alkylating agents (e.g. cyclophosphamide, chlorambucil), and systemic calcineurin inhibitors (e.g. cyclosporin, tacrolimus); OR<br>3. Any significantly immunocompromising condition(s) where, in the last 12 months the patient has received an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody treatment, but criterion 2c above is not met; OR<br>4. Others with very high-risk conditions including Down Syndrome, cerebral palsy, congenital heart disease, thalassemia, sickle cell disease and other haemoglobinopathies; OR<br>5. OR<br>Patient must have developed clinically important product-related adverse events necessitating withdrawal of statin treatment to trials of each of atorvastatin and rosuvastatin; OR<br>Patient must be contraindicated to treatment with a HMG CoA reductase inhibitor (statin) as defined in the TGA-approved Product Information; AND<br>Patient must have been treated with ezetimibe for at least 12 consecutive weeks in conjunction with a statin (if tolerated), dietary therapy and exercise; OR<br>Patient must have developed clinically important product-related adverse event/contraindication as defined in the TGA approved Product Information necessitating withdrawal of ezetimibe; AND<br>Patient must not be receiving concomitant PBS-subsidised treatment with any of: (i) another monoclonal antibody inhibiting proprotein convertase subtilisin kexin type 9 (PCSK9), (ii) inclisiran, for this PBS indication.<br>Must be treated by a specialist physician; OR<br>Must be treated by an authorised prescriber in consultation with a specialist physician.<br>Symptomatic atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is defined as:<br>(i) the presence of symptomatic coronary artery disease (prior myocardial infarction, prior revascularisation procedure, angina associated with demonstrated significant coronary artery disease (50% or greater stenosis in 1 or more coronary arteries on imaging), or positive functional testing (e.g. myocardial perfusion scanning or stress echocardiography); **About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of the *National Health (Listing of Pharmaceutical Benefits) Instrument 2024* that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 1 September 2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the ***endnotes***) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Editorial changes**

For more information about any editorial changes made in this compilation, see the endnotes.

**Presentational changes**

The *Legislation Act 2003* provides for First Parliamentary Counsel to make presentational changes to a compilation. Presentational changes are applied to give a more consistent look and feel to legislation published on the Register, and enable the user to more easily navigate those documents.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self‑repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

## Schedule 4—Circumstances, purposes, conditions and variations

Note: See sections 13, 15, 16, 19 and 23.

### Part 1—Circumstances, purposes and conditions

###### 1 Circumstances, purposes and conditions

The following table sets out:

(a) circumstances for circumstances codes, for the purposes of section 13 and 23; and

(b) purposes for purposes codes, for the purposes of sections 15 and 16; and

(c) for the purposes of section 19, information relating to how authorisation is obtained when the circumstances or conditions for writing a prescription include an authorisation requirement.

| C16350 | P16350 | CN16350 | Evolocumab | Familial heterozygous hypercholesterolaemia<br>Continuing treatment with this drug or switching treatment from any of: (i) another drug that belongs to the same pharmacological class as this drug, (ii) inclisiran<br>Patient must have previously received PBS-subsidised treatment with this drug for this condition; OR<br>Patient must have received PBS-subsidised treatment for this PBS indication with any of: (i) a drug from the same pharmacological class as this drug (ii) inclisiran; AND<br>The treatment must be in conjunction with dietary therapy and exercise; AND<br>Patient must not be receiving concomitant PBS-subsidised treatment with any of: (i) another drug that belongs to the same pharmacological class as this drug, (ii) inclisiran, for this PBS indication.<br>Must be treated by a medical practitioner; OR<br>Must be treated by a nurse practitioner in consultation with a specialist physician. | Compliance with Authority Required procedures - Streamlined Authority Code 16350 |
| C16351 | P16351 | CN16351 | Evolocumab | Non-familial hypercholesterolaemia<br>Initial treatment<br>The treatment must be in conjunction with dietary therapy and exercise; AND<br>Patient must have symptomatic atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease; AND<br>Patient must have an LDL cholesterol level in excess of 1.8 millimoles per litre; AND<br>Patient must have atherosclerotic disease in two or more vascular territories (coronary, cerebrovascular or peripheral vascular territories); OR<br>Patient must have severe multi-vessel coronary heart disease defined as at least 50% stenosis in at least two large vessels; OR<br>Patient must have had at least two major cardiovascular events (i.e. myocardial infarction, unstable angina, stroke or unplanned revascularisation) in the previous 5 years; OR<br>Patient must have diabetes mellitus with microalbuminuria; OR<br>Patient must have diabetes mellitus and be aged 60 years or more; OR<br>Patient must be an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander with diabetes mellitus; OR<br>Patient must have a Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) risk score for secondary prevention of 4 or higher; AND<br>Patient must have been treated with the maximum recommended dose of atorvastatin (80 mg daily) or rosuvastatin (40 mg daily) according to the TGA-approved Product Information or the maximum tolerated dose of atorvastatin or rosuvastatin for at least 12 consecutive weeks in conjunction with dietary therapy and exercise; OR<br>Patient must have developed clinically important product-related adverse events necessitating withdrawal of statin treatment to trials of each of atorvastatin and rosuvastatin; OR<br>Patient must be contraindicated to treatment with a HMG CoA reductase inhibitor (statin) as defined in the TGA-approved Product Information; AND<br>Patient must have been treated with ezetimibe for at least 12 consecutive weeks in conjunction with a statin (if tolerated), dietary therapy and exercise; OR<br>Patient must have developed clinically important product-related adverse event/contraindication as defined in the TGA approved Product Information necessitating withdrawal of ezetimibe; AND<br>Patient must not be receiving concomitant PBS-subsidised treatment with any of: (i) another monoclonal antibody inhibiting proprotein convertase subtilisin kexin type 9 (PCSK9), (ii) inclisiran, for this PBS indication.<br>Must be treated by a specialist physician; OR<br>Must be treated by an authorised prescriber in consultation with a specialist physician.<br>Symptomatic atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is defined as:<br>(i) the presence of symptomatic coronary artery disease (prior myocardial infarction, prior revascularisation procedure, angina associated with demonstrated significant coronary artery disease (50% or greater stenosis in 1 or more coronary arteries on imaging), or positive functional testing (e.g. myocardial perfusion scanning or stress echocardiography); or<br>(ii) the presence of symptomatic cerebrovascular disease (prior ischaemic stroke, prior revascularisation procedure, or transient ischaemic attack associated with 50% or greater stenosis in 1 or more cerebral arteries on imaging); or<br>(iii) the presence of symptomatic peripheral arterial disease (prior acute ischaemic event due to atherosclerosis, prior revascularisation procedure, or symptoms of ischaemia with evidence of significant peripheral artery disease (50% or greater stenosis in 1 or more peripheral arteries on imaging)).<br>The qualifying LDL cholesterol level following at least 12 consecutive weeks of combined treatment with a statin, ezetimibe, dietary therapy and exercise (unless treatment with a statin is contraindicated, or following completion of statin trials as described in these prescriber instructions in the event of clinically important adverse events) must be documented in the patient's medical records and must be no more than 8 weeks old.<br>A clinically important product-related adverse event is defined as follows:<br>(i) Severe myalgia (muscle symptoms without creatine kinase elevation) which is proven to be temporally associated with statin treatment; or<br>(ii) Myositis (clinically important creatine kinase elevation, with or without muscle symptoms) demonstrated by results twice the upper limit of normal on a single reading or a rising pattern on consecutive measurements and which is unexplained by other causes; or<br>(iii) Unexplained, persistent elevations of serum transaminases (greater than 3 times the upper limit of normal) during treatment with a statin.<br>If treatment with atorvastatin or rosuvastatin results in development of a clinically important product-related adverse event resulting in treatment withdrawal, the patient must be treated with the alternative statin (atorvastatin or rosuvastatin) unless there is a contraindication (e.g. prior rhabdomyolysis) to the alternative statin. This retrial should occur after a washout period of at least 4 weeks, or if the creatine kinase (CK) level is elevated, retrial should not occur until CK has returned to normal.<br>In the event of a trial of the alternative statin, it is recommended that the patient is started with the minimum dose of statin in conjunction with ezetimibe. The dose of the alternative statin should be increased not more often than every 4 weeks until the recommended or maximum tolerated dose has been reached or target LDL-c has been achieved.<br>One of the following must be documented in the patient's medical records regarding prior statin treatment:<br>(i) the patient was treated with atorvastatin 80 mg or rosuvastatin 40 mg or the maximum tolerated dose of either for 12 consecutive weeks; or<br>(ii) the doses, duration of treatment and details of adverse events experienced with trials with each of atorvastatin and rosuvastatin; or<br>(iii) the patient is contraindicated to treatment with a statin as defined in the TGA-approved Product Information.<br>One or more of the following must be documented in the patient's medical records regarding the presence of cardiovascular disease or high risk of experiencing a cardiovascular event:<br>(i) atherosclerotic disease in two or more vascular territories (coronary, cerebrovascular or peripheral vascular territories); or<br>(ii) severe multi-vessel coronary heart disease defined as at least 50% stenosis in at least two large vessels; or<br>(iii) history of at least two major cardiovascular events (i.e. myocardial infarction, unstable angina, stroke or unplanned revascularisation) in the previous 5 years; or<br>(iv) diabetes mellitus with microalbuminuria; or<br>(v) diabetes mellitus and age 60 years of more; or<br>(vi) Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander with diabetes mellitus; or<br>(vii) a Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) risk score for secondary prevention of 4 or higher<br>Patients with symptomatic atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease where LDL cholesterol cannot be measured due to hypertriglyceridaemia, may qualify under this authority application if they have a non-HDL in excess of 2.4 millimoles per litre. | Compliance with Authority Required procedures - Streamlined Authority Code 16351 |

| C16709 | P16709 | CN16709 | Etanercept | Severe active rheumatoid arthritis<br>Initial treatment - Initial 2 (change or recommencement of treatment after a break in biological medicine of less than 24 months)<br>Must be treated by a rheumatologist; or<br>Must be treated by a clinical immunologist with expertise in the management of rheumatoid arthritis.<br>Patient must have received prior PBS-subsidised treatment with a biological medicine for this condition; or<br>Patient must have received prior PBS-subsidised treatment with a biological medicine under the paediatric Severe active juvenile idiopathic arthritis/Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis indication; AND<br>Patient must not have failed to respond to previous PBS-subsidised treatment with this drug for this condition; AND<br>Patient must not have already failed/ceased to respond to PBS-subsidised biological medicine treatment for this condition 5 times; AND<br>Patient must not receive more than 16 weeks of treatment under this restriction.<br>Patient must be at least 18 years of age.<br>Patients who have received PBS-subsided treatment for paediatric Severe active juvenile idiopathic arthritis or Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis where the condition has progressed to Rheumatoid arthritis may receive treatment through this restriction using existing baseline scores.<br>Where a patient is changing from a biosimilar medicine for the treatment of this condition, the prescriber must provide baseline disease severity indicators with this application, in addition to the response assessment outlined below.<br>An adequate response to treatment is defined as:<br>an ESR no greater than 25 mm per hour or a CRP level no greater than 15 mg per L or either marker reduced by at least 20% from baseline;<br>AND either of the following:<br>(a) a reduction in the total active (swollen and tender) joint count by at least 50% from baseline, where baseline is at least 20 active joints; or<br>(b) a reduction in the number of the following active joints, from at least 4, by at least 50%:<br>(i) elbow, wrist, knee and/or ankle (assessed as swollen and tender); and/or<br>(ii) shoulder and/or hip (assessed as pain in passive movement and restriction of passive movement, where pain and limitation of movement are due to active disease and not irreversible damage such as joint destruction or bony overgrowth).<br>An application for a patient who is either changing treatment from another biological medicine to this drug or recommencing therapy with this drug after a treatment break of less than 24 months, must be accompanied with details of the evidence of a response to the patient's most recent course of PBS-subsidised biological medicine, within the timeframes specified below.<br>To demonstrate a response to treatment the application must be accompanied with the assessment of response, conducted following a minimum of 12 weeks of therapy and no later than 4 weeks from cessation of the most recent course of biological medicine. It is recommended that an application for the continuing treatment be submitted no later than 4 weeks from the date of completion of the most recent course of treatment. This is to ensure treatment continuity for those who meet the continuing restriction.<br>Where a response assessment is not conducted within the required timeframe, the patient will be deemed to have failed to respond to treatment with this drug, unless the patient has experienced a serious adverse reaction of a severity resulting in the necessity for permanent withdrawal of treatment.<br>Where the baseline active joint count is based on total active joints (i.e. more than 20 active joints), response must be determined according to the reduction in the total number of active joints.
